name: TraceTriage
description: TraceTriage: a benchmark of cost-aware checkpoint-local STOP/CONTINUE decisions in OpenROAD workflows. The full release includes tabular data, fixed splits, logs and reports. Source code: https://github.com/leisihang/TraceTriage. Derived data are CC BY-SA 4.0; upstream OpenROAD, design and platform assets retain their respective licenses.
rai:dataLimitations: Evaluation is limited to OpenROAD executions, five open design families and two platforms (ASAP7 and sky130hd). Cross-domain validity, commercial signoff and safety-critical automation are not established. See paper Appendix A.9-A.10.
rai:dataBiases: Coverage reflects selected open designs, platforms, tool versions and Bayesian-optimization configuration campaigns. Strict zero-violation labels and exclusion of runs without an observable place checkpoint introduce outcome and observability selection. No demographic population is represented.
rai:personalSensitiveInformation: The records concern software tool executions, not human subjects. Released manifests use package-relative log paths and blank history_csv/task_dir fields. The dataset is not intended to contain personal, health, demographic, political or religious information. Manifest sanitization is not a claim of an exhaustive privacy review of every raw log and report.
rai:dataUseCases: Evaluate checkpoint-local STOP/CONTINUE policies with validation-only false-stop constraints and remaining-runtime utility; train supervised triage models; study cross-design/node transfer and label budgets. Completed-run outcomes score decisions and must not be included in policy inputs. Cross-domain and signoff use are unvalidated.
rai:dataSocialImpact: Potential benefits include reduced wasted compute and reproducible engineering decision evaluation. Incorrect stopping can discard viable runs; incorrect continuation wastes resources. Use as a research benchmark and decision-support testbed, with explicit false-stop constraints, rather than automated signoff authority.

prov:wasGeneratedBy.name: OpenROAD run collection and checkpoint-prefix construction
prov:wasGeneratedBy.description: The author team executed 10 Bayesian-optimization campaigns of 5,000 attempted trials each across five designs and two platforms. Observations are actual tool-execution outputs, not fabricated or language-model-generated traces. Runs without a place checkpoint were excluded, retaining 31,572 runs and 81,041 checkpoint prefixes. Labels are rule-derived: strict_success requires final success and zero detailed-routing violations, without human annotation. Prefixes contain only evidence observable at the checkpoint, while final runtime/outcome fields are evaluation targets. Fixed CSV splits group all prefixes of a completed run, with 64,645/8,132/8,264 train/validation/test rows. See paper Appendix A.5-A.7 for collection, preprocessing and annotation details. The dataset uses the ASAP7 and sky130hd platform collateral distributed with OpenROAD-flow-scripts. The OpenROAD submodule is pinned to commit 4ee14b488230e046c2e52d9094df85ccf299ac80, corresponding to OpenROAD v2.0-16267-g4ee14b4882 as reported in the packaged logs.

citeAs: Sihang Lei, Yihang Qiu, Xueyan Zhao, Yuwei Wang, and Weiqiang Wang. TraceTriage: A Benchmark for Cost-Aware Stop-or-Continue Decisions in Delayed-Outcome Workflows. NeurIPS 2026 Evaluations and Datasets Track.
